items.markingKey: Three correct pairs of equal parts with reasons (M1 M1 M1); correct test named (A1); conclusion from corresponding parts (R1). PQ = PR, QS = SR, PS common → SSS; angles PSQ = PSR and they sum to 180°, so each is 90°.

items.stem: A small tin of paint covers 8 m² and is 10 cm tall. A similar large tin is 25 cm tall. (a) How much paint (by volume) does the large tin hold compared with the small? (b) If the small tin costs €8, explain whether a price of €50 for the large tin is good value.
items.answer: (a) 125/8 times (b) yes – you get 125/8× the paint for 25/4× the price
items.markingKey: Correct scale factor for length (A1); squared for area / cubed for volume (M1 A1); comparison per unit with conclusion (R1 C1). (a) 125/8 times (b) yes – you get 125/8× the paint for 25/4× the price

items.stem: In triangle ABC, the line through the midpoint M of AB parallel to BC meets AC at N. Prove that N is the midpoint of AC.
items.answer: Triangles AMN and ABC are similar (corresponding angles) with ratio AM/AB = 1/2, so AN = AC/2.
items.markingKey: Correct pairs of equal angles/sides with reasons (M1 M1); valid test named (A1); conclusion stated (R1); logical communication (C1). Triangles AMN and ABC are similar (corresponding angles) with ratio AM/AB = 1/2, so AN = AC/2.

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "similar figures".
items.answer: Figures with the same shape: corresponding angles equal and corresponding sides in the same ratio
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: figures with the same shape: corresponding angles equal and corresponding sides in the same ratio. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT a valid congruence test for triangles?
options: AAA
RHS
SAS
SSS
items.answer: AAA
items.markingKey: A. AAA only proves similarity: triangles can have equal angles but different sizes.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "area scale factor"?
options: The square of the length scale factor, k², by which areas are multiplied in an enlargement
Figures with the same shape: corresponding angles equal and corresponding sides in the same ratio
Two angles and the side between them equal in both triangles
A logical argument in which each step follows from definitions, given facts or previously proven results
items.answer: The square of the length scale factor, k², by which areas are multiplied in an enlargement
items.markingKey: A. "area scale factor" is the square of the length scale factor, k², by which areas are multiplied in an enlargement.

items.stem: Explain why the statement "all equilateral triangles are similar" is true but "all isosceles triangles are similar" is false.
items.answer: Equilateral triangles all have angles 60°, 60°, 60°; isosceles triangles can have different apex angles.
items.markingKey: Equilateral triangles all have angles 60°, 60°, 60°; isosceles triangles can have different apex angles. (R1 R1)

items.stem: Rectangle A is 6 cm by 10 cm and rectangle B is 12 cm by 16 cm. Explain whether the rectangles are similar.
items.answer: not similar
items.markingKey: Compare ratios: 12/6 = 2 and 16/10 = 8/5 (M1); not equal so not similar (R1).

items.stem: Mei says two triangles with sides 6 cm and 6 cm and a 50° angle (not between those sides) must be congruent. Explain why this is not necessarily true.
items.answer: SSA is not a congruence test
items.markingKey: The angle is not included, so the third side can take two positions (ambiguous case) (R1); a sketch or example of two different triangles (R1).

items.stem: A cube is enlarged by scale factor 5. Priya says its surface area and volume are both multiplied by 5. Explain why this is wrong and give the correct factors.
items.answer: area × 25, volume × 125
items.markingKey: Area involves two lengths → k² = 25 (R1); volume three lengths → k³ = 125 (R1).

items.stem: Explain why proving two triangles similar is enough to find a missing length but not enough to show two lengths are equal.
items.answer: Similarity fixes ratios, not sizes; equal lengths need a scale factor of 1, i.e. congruence.
items.markingKey: Similarity fixes ratios, not sizes; equal lengths need a scale factor of 1, i.e. congruence. (R1 R1)

items.stem: Rectangle A is 3 cm by 12 cm and rectangle B is 6 cm by 15 cm. Explain whether the rectangles are similar.
items.answer: not similar
items.markingKey: Compare ratios: 6/3 = 2 and 15/12 = 5/4 (M1); not equal so not similar (R1).

items.stem: Amara writes: "In SAS the angle can be any angle of the triangle." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The angle must be the included angle, between the two given sides.
items.markingKey: The angle must be the included angle, between the two given sides. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Two similar bottles have heights 12 cm and 18 cm. The smaller holds 480 ml. How much does the larger hold?
items.markingKey: Length factor 3/2; volume factor (3/2)³ = 27/8 (M1 A1); 1620 ml (A1).

items.stem: The exterior angle at C of triangle ABC is 94° and angle A = 55°. Find angle B, giving a reason.
items.answer: 39° (exterior angle = sum of the two interior opposite angles)
items.markingKey: 39° (exterior angle = sum of the two interior opposite angles): A1 value(s), R1 reason(s).

items.stem: Ana, who is 1.8 m tall, casts a shadow 3.0 m long. At the same time a tree casts a shadow 20 m long. How tall is the tree?
items.markingKey: Similar triangles identified (R1); correct ratio set up (M1); 12 m (A1).

items.stem: Triangle ABC has sides 8, 9 and 15 cm; triangle DEF has sides 9, 15 and 8 cm. Are they congruent? Name the test.
items.answer: congruent (SSS)
items.markingKey: congruent (SSS) (A1); correct matching of corresponding parts stated (R1).

items.stem: Two similar bottles have heights 18 cm and 24 cm. The smaller holds 280 ml. How much does the larger hold?
items.markingKey: Length factor 4/3; volume factor (4/3)³ = 64/27 (M1 A1); 663.7 ml (A1).

items.stem: The exterior angle at C of triangle ABC is 114° and angle A = 43°. Find angle B, giving a reason.
items.answer: 71° (exterior angle = sum of the two interior opposite angles)
items.markingKey: 71° (exterior angle = sum of the two interior opposite angles): A1 value(s), R1 reason(s).

items.stem: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC with DE parallel to BC. AD = 6 cm, DB = 6 cm and DE = 9 cm. (a) Prove that triangles ADE and ABC are similar. (b) Find BC. (c) Find the ratio of the area of ADE to the area of ABC.
items.markingKey: (a) angle A common; corresponding angles ADE = ABC (DE ∥ BC) → AA (R1 R1). (b) BC/DE = 12/6 (M1) → 18 cm (A1). (c) area ratio = (length ratio)² = 36:144 (A1).

items.stem: Two ladders of equal length 12 m lean against parallel walls, each making 60° with the ground. Prove that they reach the same height and find it.
items.answer: ASA/AAS congruent right triangles; height 10.4 m
items.markingKey: Congruence test stated with three equal parts (R1 R1); calculation (M1 A1); communicated clearly (C1). ASA/AAS congruent right triangles; height 10.4 m

items.stem: A pizza of diameter 20 cm costs $7. A similar pizza of diameter 50 cm costs $26.25. Which is better value per cm²? Show your reasoning.
items.answer: large pizza: $2.23 vs $1.34 per 100 cm²
items.markingKey: Correct scale factor for length (A1); squared for area / cubed for volume (M1 A1); comparison per unit with conclusion (R1 C1). large pizza: $2.23 vs $1.34 per 100 cm²

items.stem: In triangle ABC, AD bisects angle A and AD ⊥ BC. Prove that triangle ABC is isosceles.
items.answer: Triangles ABD and ACD: angle BAD = CAD, AD common, angles at D both 90° → ASA, so AB = AC.
items.markingKey: Key construction/identification (M1); equal parts with reasons (M1 M1); conclusion (R1); logical presentation (C1). Triangles ABD and ACD: angle BAD = CAD, AD common, angles at D both 90° → ASA, so AB = AC.
